title: How few colours for the plaza?
hook: A plaza with six regions. Surely three colours keep every neighbour different?

knows: backtracking tries a choice and undoes it on a dead end (four-queens-pruning)
doesNotKnow: that a hub linked to an odd ring of regions cannot be coloured with three colours

misconception: Three colours are enough for any map with a handful of regions.
objective: The learner can explain that the centre region uses one colour, so the five ring regions must alternate two colours round an odd ring, which fails; backtracking finds no 3-colouring and a fourth colour is needed, while a ring of four needs only three.

claims.text: A centre region touching five ring regions, each also touching its two ring neighbours, cannot be coloured with three colours so that touching regions differ; four colours suffice.
claims.source: Builder's Node brute-force backtracking colourer on the 5-wheel (hub + 5-cycle), 2026-10-14: k=2 and k=3 fail, k=4 succeeds (C, 1..5 = 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4). Same backtrack() as Demo.tsx (regions C, 1..5 in order, colours tried in order). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own backtracker (fc21/wh.mjs) and an order-free exhaustive search over all k^6 colourings: chromatic number of the 5-wheel is 4; backtrack(4) gives C,1..5 = 1,2,3,2,3,4.

claims.text: The centre takes one colour, so the ring regions have only two left; two colours must alternate round the ring, and with five (an odd number) the last region meets both.
claims.source: Every ring region touches the centre, so none can share its colour. A cycle 2-coloured must alternate; an odd cycle returns to its start on the same parity, so its last vertex is adjacent to both colours. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Odd-cycle argument checked; the same exhaustive search shows the 5-cycle has no 2-colouring.

claims.text: Backtracking with three colours (regions C, 1 to 5 in order, colours in order) hits 6 dead ends and finds no colouring; its first dead end is region 5 after C, 1, 2, 3, 4 take red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow.
claims.source: Demo.tsx THREE = backtrack(3); builder re-ran the same search in Node (2026-10-14): 6 dead ends, 27 placements, first dead end at region 5 with colours [1,2,3,2,3]. The count depends on the region and colour order shown. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Same search order as Demo.tsx: k = 3 -> 6 dead ends, 27 placements, first dead end region 5 with C..4 = red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow.

claims.text: With four regions round the centre, three colours are enough: the ring's two colours alternate all the way round, and because four is even the last region meets only one of them. Backtracking with four colours allowed (regions C, 1 to 4, colours in order) finds red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow, using 3.
claims.source: Builder's Node backtracking run on the 4-wheel (hub + 4-cycle), 2026-10-14: k=2 fails, k=3 succeeds (1, 2, 3, 2, 3). Derivation: an even ring alternates two colours. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): 4-wheel: backtrack(3) succeeds (1,2,3,2,3), exhaustive chromatic number 3. | Builder revision v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): now shown on stage: a 'Ring of 4' control re-runs the same backtracking on a 4-ring; the stage line reads 'Ring of 4, 4 colours: backtracking found a colouring using 3.' and the runs line '4 ring: done, 3 used'. Builder trace of backtrack(4, 4) in Demo.tsx: C=0, 1=1, 2=2, 3=1, 4=2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): DISPUTED. Numbers hold: own node backtrack(4,3) and backtrack(4,4) both give red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow (3 used). But a reachable branch makes the reveal false: with 4 colours and Ring of 4 chosen while colouring by hand, paint C red, 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 purple, 4 yellow (valid, 4 used). after() stores seen['4-4'] = {ok, used 4}; a later Run backtracking on that ring reaches ring-of-four (used 3) but setSeen keeps the first ok record. The reveal then says 'On the ring of four the two colours alternated all the way round: done with 4 colours' and the runs line '4 ring: done, 4 used'. Fix (builder): record only colourings using <= 3 colours for the ring-of-four record (or keep the smallest 'used' per key), so the quoted run is the one that reached the milestone. | Builder revision v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, W-231): the ring-of-four record now keeps the finished run that used the fewest colours (a later 3-colour run replaces an earlier 4-colour hand colouring), and the reveal quotes the ring of four only when that record used 3 or fewer. The runs line shows the same fewest-colours record. Claim text unchanged.

claims.text: For big maps no fast method is known for finding the fewest colours, so trying and undoing is often the tool.
claims.source: Deciding k-colourability (chromatic number) is NP-complete: Karp (1972), 'Reducibility among combinatorial problems' (chromatic number is one of the 21 problems); CLRS 4e ch. 34 (graph colouring as an NP-complete problem). Citations from the brief, check before verifying. 'Map' here means the regions-touching graph of the stage, not only planar maps; for planar maps 4 colours always suffice (four colour theorem), but finding the minimum (3-colourability of planar graphs) is still NP-complete (Garey, Johnson and Stockmeyer 1976; check). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Karp 1972 (chromatic number among the 21) and CLRS ch. 34 not opened; both match my knowledge. Garey, Johnson and Stockmeyer, 'Some simplified NP-complete graph problems', Theoretical Computer Science 1 (1976) 237-267, planar 3-colourability NP-complete: corroborated by web search (Academia record, TAMU lecture notes). 'No fast method is known' is an accurate reading of NP-hardness.

claims.text: On the ring of five with four colours, backtracking (same order) colours C, 1 to 5 red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow, purple, using all 4.
claims.source: Demo.tsx backtrack(5, 4); matches the build note's node re-run (1,2,3,2,3,4). Stage text 'Ring of 5, 4 colours: backtracking found a colouring using 4.' Builder statement, not self-verified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node backtrack(5,4): C, 1..5 = red, blue, yellow, blue, yellow, purple, 0 dead ends, 4 used; backtrack(5,3): 6 dead ends, stuck at region 5. Any valid colouring of the 5-wheel uses 4, so the s54 record is 4 on every branch.

recall.question: A centre region is ringed by seven regions, each touching the centre and its two neighbours. Fewest colours so touching regions differ?
recall.why: The centre takes one colour, so the ring must alternate two. Seven is odd, so the last ring region meets both and needs a fourth colour.
